intervals.label: proposal and design studies
intervals.note: Month from the 2026 project talk (2011.12); Physics World says it was first proposed in 2011 by Zhao Guangda. Design documents: Physics & Detector CDR (arXiv:2303.15790, 2023), accelerator CDR (arXiv:2509.11522, 2025). The accelerator CDR 'aims to secure support from the Chinese central government for its construction during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030)'; the June 2026 talk says the proposal was submitted in 2025 and defended for inclusion in that plan. No approval is reported in the sources fetched (as of 2026-10-26).

name: STCF Collaboration
notes: Group sizes differ between sources: about 500 scientists from 74 institutes (Physics World), 82 institutions and 453 authors (talk), 438 authors on the arXiv listing of the CDR.

summary.plain: The international group of about 500 scientists from 74 institutes in Asia, Europe and the United States working on the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility in Hefei, led by the University of Science and Technology of China.
summary.technical: STCF Collaboration (the 'STCF working group'): about 500 scientists from 74 universities and research institutes (Physics World, undated); 82 institutions and 453 authors on the Physics & Detector CDR (DIS2024 talk; arXiv:2303.15790 lists 438 authors). Membership list not retrieved.
